title: Debugging: fix Byte's programs
reflection: Which bug was hardest to find? How did you find it?

steps.goal: Your Byte has three new programs. Start with broken_row: run it, read the error, and fix it so that it builds a row of 6 blocks.
steps.block_goal: MINE has put three broken programs among your programs (the "My programs" menu). Start with broken_row: run it, watch Byte, and fix it so that it builds a row of 6 blocks.
steps.not_yet: Not yet: the row needs 6 blocks in a straight line. Does broken_row still stop with an error?
hints: Read the error: the number after the program's name is the line where Lua stopped. Open the program with edit broken_row and go to that line.
Lua tells capital and small letters apart: compare that line with the instructions you used in the loops lesson.
block_hints: Watch where the block ends up: in front of Byte, in the air. Which block decides where the blocks go?
The place a block block has a menu: in front, above, below. Which one makes a row on the ground?

steps.goal: Now broken_floor: Lua won't even start it. Fix it so that it builds a floor 4 blocks long and 3 wide.
steps.block_goal: Now broken_floor: it builds, but the wrong shape. Fix it so that it builds a floor 4 blocks long and 3 wide.
steps.not_yet: Not yet: the floor must be 4 blocks long and 3 wide, 12 blocks in all.
hints: The message says "Expected end": something was opened and never closed. Every for needs its own end.
Lua points at line 3, but the missing end belongs to another loop. Which loop isn't closed? The indentation helps.
block_hints: Read MINE's measurements: the floor is 3 tall, so every row is one block higher than the one before. Which block makes Byte go up?
move up must happen once, before the rows: drag it out of the repeat and put it above it.

steps.goal: Last one: broken_square runs without errors, but it should build a square 4 × 4. Run it, look at what it builds, and fix it.
steps.block_goal: Last one: broken_square should build a square 4 × 4. Run it, look at what it builds, and fix it.
steps.not_yet: Not yet: the square must be 4 blocks long and 4 wide, 16 blocks in all.
hints: No error message this time: compare what Byte built with the goal. How many blocks are in one row?
Each row has two loops, one going forward and one coming back: they must repeat the same number of times.
block_hints: Compare what Byte built with the goal: how many blocks are in one row?
Each row has two repeat blocks, one going forward and one coming back: they must repeat the same number of times.
